thread:
alex: Hey team — spinning up a short internal lab to pick sane defaults for RPM/TPM + burst windows. We've had multiple support tickets where small clients hit 429s under short spikes and others complain about latency during hour-long churn. wanna hammer on patterns and land a recommendation by EOD.

jenna: +1. want to cover two profiles: steady medium (50–200 users) and short sharp spikes (bursting to thousands for ~2–5m). Also need to validate per-key vs per-project quotas.

ron: Can we reuse the k6 scripts from last year's churn tests? I still have the scenarios folder. will tune ramp patterns.

alex: Yep reuse and tweak. Primary metrics: 95/99 P50 latency, 429 rate, request queue depth on gateway, and CPU/GPU util on serving nodes. Secondary: billing anomalies (unexpected token accounting on retries).

lia: Important: include auth edgecases — expired tokens, rate-limited token refresh loops. Those caused a cascade last month.

infra-bot: NOTE: test cluster 'lab-rate-3' scheduled from 2025-03-10 15:00 UTC for 90m. If you need more, open infra ticket.

support-ed: I'll patch in a repro case from the customer where they saw 12% 429s with 1.2k RPM sustained for 7m. It looks like they were using short lived client processes that retried aggressively.

sre-sam: Quick proposal for baseline defaults: per-key RPM=600, burst window=60s with burst capacity=3x (i.e., allow 1800 reqs in a 60s window), token replenish = RPM/60. For TPM (tokens per minute) translate accordingly. But we should validate.

jenna: That 3x burst feels high for multi-tenant. Maybe 2x default and a higher tier for reserved capacity. If we set default 2x, that means 1200 reqs per 60s at 600rpm.

alex: Agreed on tiering. Default conservative; reserved/dedicated customers get large burst. But support needs guidance on when to escalate to Dedicated.

ron: Test plan I'm going to run (k6):
```
scenarios: {
  steady: { executor: constant-vus, vus: 50, duration: '20m' },
  burst: { executor: ramping-arrival-rate, startRate: 50, timeUnit: '1s', preAllocatedVUs: 200, stages: [{target:2000, duration:'30s'},{target:2000,duration:'4m'},{target:0,duration:'30s'}] }
}
thresholds: {
  http_req_failed: ['rate<0.01'],
  http_req_duration: ['p(95)<800']
}
```

ron: Will run per-key and per-project variants.

lia: Also add a test where token refresh loop does exponential backoff disabled. ie client retries on 401 -> immediate refresh -> another 401 -> flood.

support-ed: For billing we need to validate how we count retries. Current rule: each successful tokenization/generation call counts tokens; error 429 does not bill. But retries that succeed will bill cumulative tokens — customers often double-report cost increases. Capture sample logs.

alex: Good call. ron, can you capture request ids and correlate with billing events? We should produce a short CSV mapping req_id,timestamp,status,tokens_billed.

ron: Yep. I'll grep logs and attach a snippet here.

ron: Paste from a burst run (sanitized):
```
2025-03-10T15:12:34Z req=abc123 key=teamA status=200 tokens=152 duration_ms=120
2025-03-10T15:12:34Z req=abc124 key=teamA status=429 tokens=0 duration_ms=5
2025-03-10T15:12:35Z req=abc125 key=teamA status=200 tokens=148 duration_ms=130
2025-03-10T15:12:36Z req=abc126 key=teamA status=200 tokens=160 duration_ms=140
```

ron: Observed: ~6% 429 during ramp to 2k RPS when default throttles kicked. Median latency stayed ~130ms for successful calls, p99 jumped to 900ms for some tails.

jenna: Are the 429s clustered per key? If a single key hit the cap, others should be fine.

ron: Yes clusters per key. With per-project cap higher, same key still hit its per-key limits and clients retried sequentially causing more pile-up.

sre-sam: Two operational knobs to avoid customer pain: 1) short adaptive backoff hint in 429 response header (Retry-After with jitter suggestion), 2) soft QoS: start shedding long-running low-priority requests during burst.

alex: Let's prototype adding X-RateLimit-Reset and X-Backoff-Suggest headers so clients get deterministic hints.

lia: For auth workout: I forced a run where refresh token endpoint returned 500 for 30s. Clients that retried immediately produced a client storm. Need to add guidance in docs: exponential backoff starting at 200ms up to 5s for auth refresh.

support-ed: I'll draft a KB article for customers: recommended SDK defaults include jittered exp backoff and queue length checks. Also mention how to interpret 429 vs 503 in our platform.

jenna: Results summary after 3 runs:
- scenario steady (50 vus): 0% 429, p95=110ms
- burst small (to 800rps): 0.8% 429, p95=180ms
- burst large (to 2k arrival): 5–8% 429 for default per-key 600rpm/2x burst, p99 spikes to 900–1200ms

alex: Actionable recs:
- Default per-key RPM=600, default burst multiplier=2 (window 60s) -> conservative safety
- Add optional per-key burst=3 for higher-tier/enterprise
- Default SDK: enable jittered exp backoff (base=200ms, cap=5s)
- Add Retry-After and Backoff hint headers in gateway
- Update support runbook: how to pull req_id -> billing map

sre-sam: Also add a Canary: increase default burst to 2.5 for 2 weeks in staging to validate fewer false positives then roll.

alex: Good. jenna, ron, lia — can you produce a one-page runbook + sample k6 scenario + log grep commands by EOD? We want it in product runbooks and support KB.

jenna: On it. will push gist with scripts.

ron: I'll attach CSVs and grep snippets after final run.

lia: I'll craft the auth-backoff blurb.

infra-bot: ARTIFACT: lab-report-1825009876 uploaded to /mnt/lab-reports/1825009876.csv

alex: Thanks all. If anyone else wants to reproduce, use lab-rate-3 and ping infra to extend. Closing thread when runbook is in PR. :thumbsup:
